How confidence is setIt follows the kind of evidence, not judgement.
  • The customer's own statement (high confidence at most): The organisation says so itself: its press release, website, annual report or a named executive on the record.
  • Regulatory or securities filing (high confidence at most): A filing by the customer or the vendor names the relationship.
  • Independent press (high confidence at most): Editorially independent reporting describes the deployment.
  • Joint announcement (medium confidence at most): A press release issued with the vendor, usually with a quote from the customer.
  • Vendor case study (medium confidence at most): The vendor's published customer story naming the organisation.
  • Vendor mention only (low confidence at most): A logo, a customer list or a passing mention by the vendor, with nothing from the customer.
  • An organisation that also holds a stake in the vendor is labelled “Investor and customer” and is never rated above medium.
  • A partnership is listed as a partner, not a customer.

Timeline

  1. 2026-11-10 · vulnerability disclosure Fortinet
    Fortinet discloses two critical routing-daemon flaws affecting FortiOS and FortiSASE

    According to Fortinet PSIRT advisories FG-IR-26-267 and FG-IR-26-268, published on 10 November 2026, FortiOS and FortiSASE are affected by CVE-2026-126253, an authentication bypass in the OSPF daemon rated CVSS 9.3, and CVE-2026-126254, a numeric truncation error in the BGP daemon rated CVSS 9.6 that an authenticated iBGP neighbour could use to cause denial of service. The advisories say FortiSASE 26.3.1 was remediated in 26.3.2 with no customer action, list FortiSASE 25.1 to 26.2 as needing migration to a fixed release, and mark both flaws as not known to be exploited. Fortinet FortiGuard Labs (vendor, retrieved 2026-11-22, opens in new tab)Fortinet FortiGuard Labs (vendor, retrieved 2026-11-22, opens in new tab)

  2. 2026-01-27 · security incident Fortinet
    Fortinet discloses exploited FortiCloud SSO authentication bypass, CVE-2026-24858

    Disclosed by Fortinet on 2026-01-27 in advisory FG-IR-26-060: a critical authentication bypass in FortiCloud single sign-on let an attacker with a FortiCloud account log in to devices registered to other accounts where that sign-on was enabled, and was exploited in the wild by two malicious FortiCloud accounts, which Fortinet locked on 22 January. Fortinet disabled FortiCloud SSO on 26 January and restored it the next day with vulnerable versions blocked. Affected products are FortiOS, FortiManager, FortiAnalyzer, FortiProxy, FortiSwitchManager, FortiWeb and FortiNAC-F; FortiSASE is not listed and the advisory says FortiGate Cloud, FortiManager Cloud and FortiAnalyzer Cloud were not affected. CSO Online reported on 2026-01-28 that customers had seen administrator accounts created on fully patched devices and that the US cybersecurity agency added the flaw to its exploited-vulnerabilities catalogue. Fortinet FortiGuard Labs (vendor, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)CSO Online (independent press, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)

  3. 2025-09-22 · litigation Fortinet
    Securities class action filed against Fortinet over FortiGate refresh-cycle statements

    Disclosed in Fortinet's Form 10-Q filed 2026-10-30, whose litigation data labels name Oklahoma Firefighters Pension and Retirement System v. Fortinet Inc. et al. Plaintiff counsel's case page says the complaint was filed on 22 September 2025 in the US District Court for the Northern District of California (case 25-cv-08037), covers purchases from 8 November 2024 to 6 August 2025, and alleges misleading statements about the 2025-2026 FortiGate refresh cycle; a consolidated complaint is dated 24 April 2026. The allegations are untested and no ruling was found. The text of Fortinet's own litigation note could not be read. US Securities and Exchange Commission (EDGAR) (primary filing, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)Bernstein Litowitz Berger & Grossmann LLP (other, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)

  4. 2024-08-01 · acquisition Fortinet
    Fortinet completes acquisition of cloud security firm Lacework

    Fortinet announced on 2 August 2024 that it had completed its acquisition of Lacework, a cloud-native application protection platform company, effective 1 August 2024. The price was not disclosed in the release. The Lacework platform is now sold as FortiCNAPP. Recorded because it changed the product's ownership.
